scope: New HTTP framing, byte partitioning and claim scope only. No network download, Torch, GPU, model, service or closed-component review.

findings.title: Flattening response headers loses contradictory framing
findings.verified_reproduction: Using actual stdlib http.client.HTTPResponse on an in-memory fake socket (no network), both Content-Length:10 plus Content-Length:999, and Transfer-Encoding:chunked plus Content-Length:10, pass the current header capture/check_headers,10-byte readinto and finalEOF checks. Both test bodies decode to exactly0123456789.
findings.impact: Decoded payload remains bounded and fully compared. However, the claimed exact HTTP framing validation accepts contradictory raw headers and omits that contradiction from the evidence.
findings.focused_fix: Capture raw header multiplicity before flattening. Reject duplicate Content-Range/Content-Length/Content-Encoding and any Transfer-Encoding in this deliberately exact Content-Length contract; add the two no-network HTTPResponse controls. No full gate cycle needed.

limits: Byte equality across four responses does not authenticate an entire5.36GB shard; whole_shard_verified remainsfalse.
Two observations perarm support only the reported diagnostic ratio, not a confidence interval, connection-count causal claim, full-shard throughput guarantee or serving/model performance.

Timed arm includes buffer allocation/thread-pool/HTTP work, and excludes the subsequent SHA calculation. Freeze/containment orchestration is still being prepared and was not submitted in this bounded scope.
